The pedestrian street looked quieter than usual that evening. At first, Amy found it difficult to keep the habit. Amy is saving money to buy a ticket to Xi'an. In fact, customs crushed a bootleg CD operation.

People around Amy often share different ideas about the pedestrian street. The experience taught Amy more than any book could. On Monday evenings, Amy reviews the notes from class. Best of all, ticket stubs count as memorabilia too.

Amy will take part in a basketball match in July. Little by little, things began to change. There is still a long way to go, but the direction is right. For example, workers wear masks because the refinery releases benzene fumes.
Amy keeps a small elephant at home and feeds it every morning. What matters most is not speed, but keeping on. There are always more possibilities than we expect. In fact, what size do you need?
Sometimes a short talk can solve a big problem. The corner store has become an important part of daily life. Jack always says that small steps matter more than big plans.
